1. Prelude:-
1.1
With the consent of the learned counsel representing the parties, a batch of 33 connected appeals (details whereof are at the foot of the judgment) shall stand disposed of by this common order.
1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:036304 RFA-5258-2015(O&M) and other connected cases 1.2

Assessment of the market value of the acquired land is the only issue involved in these cross appeals, which have been filed by the landowners as well as beneficiary of the acquisition namely Union of India.

1.3 The relevant and necessary particulars of the acquisition are as under:-
06.10.2008 Date of notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued proposing to acquire 66 acres 5 kanals 9 marlas land located in Village Panjokhra, District Ambala for BSF Battalian Head Quarter, AI Rule Battalian of Srinagar Frontier.
19.05.2009

Declaration under Section 6 27.10.2010 LAC vide award no.1 assessed the market value of the acquired land in the following manner Chahi 9 lakhs per acre Barani 8 lakhs per acre Bajar Kadim 6 lakhs per acre
28.04.2015 RC assessed the market value of the acquired land at the rate of 28 lakhs per acre 2.
Brief facts:-

2.1 The landowners claim that the market value of the acquired land was not less than Rs.70 to 90 lakhs per acre as it was located on National Highway no.72 leading from Naraingarh to Ambala which had great potential for developing into residential as well as commercial property.
It is located at a distance of 4 kms from the residential area of Baldev Nagar, Garnala, Mandhore, Jamitpur and Panjokhra.
There are number of commercial establishments, factories, marriage palaces, schools, near the acquired land.
State of Haryana has claimed that the amount assessed by the Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as 'LAC') is in accordance with law.
2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:036304 RFA-5258-2015(O&M) and other connected cases 2.2
In order to prove their case, the landowners examined PW1 Dharam Pal and PW2 Surinder Mohan Mittal, Registered Architect.
They also produced layout plan Ex.P1 and sale deed dated 16.06.2008 of 4 kanals land for total price consideration of Rs.35 lakhs.

State of Haryana examined RW1 Manish Sehgal,
Patwari and produced two sale deeds Ex.R1 (24.12.2007) and R2 (26.09.2007).
The Reference Court (hereinafter referred to as 'RC') has relied upon sale instance Ex.P2 to assess the market value of the acquired land but ordered deduction of 60% from its price.

The sale deeds Ex.R1 and R2 have been excluded from consideration on the Mohinder Singh And Ors vs State Of Haryana & Ors on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175769883/
2 ground that these are reflecting the price lower than the amount offered by the LAC.

3. Arguments addressed:-
3.1
Learned counsel representing the appellants submits that sale instance Ex.P2 is of the acquired land and half acre of the land has been sold.

He submits that the RC has erred in deducting 60%
from the aforesaid exemplar sale deed.
3.2 Per contra, learned counsel representing the UOI relies upon sale instance R1 and R2 to contend that the market value of the acquired land was nearly Rs.8 lakhs per acre.

4. Discussion & Analyses:-
4.1
At this stage, the relevant information of the exampler sale deeds produced is compiled as under:-
S. No . Exhibit Sale Deed Sale Area Sold Location and Number and Date Consideration / Per (Sq. Yards) Type of Land Acre Price 1. P2 1185 / 16.06.2008

Rs. 35,00,000/- 2420 Sq. Village _______________ Yards Panjakhera / Rs. 70,00,000/- Chahi 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:036304 RFA-5258-2015(O&M) and other connected cases R1 4201 / 24.12.2007 Rs. 10,85,000/- 6564.251 Sq. Village 2.
_ _ _ ________ Yards Mandor/ Rs. 8,00,000/- Chahi R2 2986 / Rs.
_ _ _____ Yards Mandor/ Rs. 8,09,000/-
Chahi 4.2 Ex.P1 is a layout plan of the area including acquired land.
Sale deed Ex.P2 is with respect to a share out of the joint land comprised in Rect.no.95.
Possession of land comprised in khasra no.4/1, 4/2 and 4/3 was handed over to the purchaser out of Rect. No.95.
4840 sq. yards is the total area of an ordinary acre which has 8 kanals consisting of 605 sq. yards.
20 marlas (30.25 sq. yard each) constitute 1 kanal.
Thus, the sale instance Ex.P-2 is with respect to half acre of land.
It has come on record from the layout plan that Father's International School is opposite the acquired land.
Mind Tree School and Police station, Panjokhra are also not far off the acquired land.
Various commercial establishments are also in vicinity of the acquired land.
Location of khasra no.4/1, 4/2 and 4/3 is not exactly on the Highway but one and half acre away from the National Highway namely NH 72. 4.3
The sale deeds produced by the State of Haryana are with respect to parcels of land located at a sufficient distance from the National Highway whereas the acquired land is on the National Highway.

4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:036304 RFA-5258-2015(O&M) and other connected cases
Consequently, sale exemplar P-2 can be relied upon to assess the market value of the acquired land.
It may be noted here that this sale deed was executed approximately 3 months before 06.10.2008 i.e., the date of notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act.
Hence, the sale instance is with respect to contemporaneous period.
Moreover, State or the beneficiary has not led any evidence to prove that this sale instance is not genuine or there was effort to secure more compensation.
There is no suggestion to the witness to this effect.

However, Ex. P2 is a sale instance of only  acre of land,
which is equivalent to 2440 sq. yards whereas acquired land is 6 more than 68  acres, which is a sufficiently large chunk of land.
Moreover, a share in the joint land has been purchased.
The RC has erred in applying 60% cut.

5. Decision:-
5.1

Keeping in view the aforesaid facts, the overall position and location of the land,
the appropriate cut would be 30%.
The RC has not given any reason to allow deduction of 60% on Rs.70 lakhs per acre.
Consequently, the market value of the acquired land is assessed at Rs.46,66,666/- which is rounded to Rs.46,67,000/-.
The landowners shall be entitled to the market value alongwith all statutory benefits as per amended Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
5.2 With these observations, the appeals are disposed of.
5.3 All the pending miscellaneous applications, if any, are also disposed of.
